title: VPC pilot economics playbook + CISO/ops scripting
content:
TL;DR:
- One-pager and playbook for running a short on-prem/VPC pilot with regulated buyers (CISO, infra, procurement). Focus: predictable economics, minimal control-plane exposure options, measurable risk reduction.

Primary positioning statements (short):
- "Redwood runs where you run it" -> emphasize single API/rollout and telemetry model while letting the company keep data custody.
- Control-plane-as-coordination, not control: frame the control plane as a lightweight orchestration & telemetry conduit that can be minimized or customer-hosted for auditors.
- Pilot promise: 8-week technical pilot, <30ms median inference to app network, cost visibility dashboard, and a runbook for data egress proofs.

Control plane language — options to use in narrow order of customer comfort:
1) "Hosted coordination plane (opt-in)": describes default managed experience but call out optional disablement.
2) "Customer-managed orchestration endpoint": highlights the same API surface but hosted in customer VPC for full audit trail.
3) "Air-gapped control bundle": for extreme regulated buyers, mention an on-prem binary and signed attestation model.

Why this framing works: reduces mental model of "Redwood controls my data" -> shifts to "Redwood provides tooling; you choose custody model".

Top buyer objections and concise rebuttals (copyable lines):
- Objection: "We can't allow an external control plane to send metadata or telemetry."
  Rebuttal: "We surfaced two hardened options: customer-managed control endpoint (VPC) or an offline control bundle. For the pilot we can run with telemetry off and a daily signed artifact for health checks—no live metadata leaves your network."
- Objection: "What about auditability — can auditors see the exact evidence?"
  Rebuttal: "Yes. We provide an artifacts bundle (signed logs, model version manifest, crypto hashes) and a reproducible runbook so you can demonstrate exactly what model binary was invoked and when."
- Objection: "We're worried about vendor lock and exit costs."
  Rebuttal: "Pilot ends with a 'handover pack' — configs, quantized model artifacts, and a decommission checklist so you can migrate or self-host without hidden steps."

Pilot ask (what to ask the customer to commit to):
- 8 weeks pilot duration (4 weeks integration + 4 weeks traffic validation).
- A single app/team as pilot owner (product + infra contact).
- Access: customer-owned VPC peering or site-to-site VPN, minimal firewall rule for model serving ports, and a service account for deployment (read-only by default).
- Security gating: SOC2 or equivalent evidence acceptable, or signed supply-chain artifacts for air-gapped run.

Pilot success metrics (shared dashboard):
- Functional: end-to-end request success rate >= 99.5% for pilot workload.
- Latency: p50 < agreed SLO (usually 50–200ms depending on model/region), p95 < 2x p50.
- Cost: measured $/1k inference tokens relative to hosted baseline and projected 12-mo run rate.
- Ops: mean time to rollback < 5 minutes using our canary rollback steps.
- Security: evidence bundle validated by customer audit team within pilot window.

Economic justification model (talking points for procurement/finance):
- Show three columns: hosted baseline unit cost, dedicated-reserved estimate (30–45% lower on committed capacity), and projected private on-prem cost (includes infra amortization). Use a 12–18 month horizon.
- Emphasize predictable unit economics: reserved GPUs + batching = clear per-token floor.
- Negotiable levers: commit length (12/24/36), telemetry retention and retention tier (impacts pricing), optional managed service for backups/patching.

Negotiation levers and concessions (playbook for AE):
- Give a 90-day discounted managed setup fee if customer signs pilot within 2 weeks.
- For procurement pushback on SLAs, offer a pilot-specific SLA with credit-based remedies and a documented escalation path.
- For customers insistent on no outbound control plane, offer reduced-price 'control-plane handover' professional services to ship an air-gapped bundle.

CISO/infra scripts and sticky lines (for early meeting):
- "We treat the control plane as a coordination surface — it does not store customer payloads. For compliance we can run a configuration where telemetry is aggregated and redacted, or entirely customer-hosted."
- "We deliver signed model manifests and hashes so your auditors can verify the exact build used in production."
- "Our pilot removes unknowns: we'll run a runbook that your team can replay and verify."

Sample short outreach email (CISO):
Subject: Pilot proposal — private inference with verifiable audit artifacts
Hi [Name],
We'd like to propose an 8-week pilot to run private inference for [app/team]. The pilot gives you: customer-owned VPC deployment, signed model and audit artifacts, and a cost/latency dashboard tied to pilot metrics. If useful I can share a 1-page runbook and kickoff agenda for your infra and audit teams.
Best,
Aisha

Follow-up (ops technical contact) quick checklist to send after kickoff: 
- VPN/peer details and firewall rule sample
- Service account artifact and least-privilege policy
- Expected pilot dataset(s) and redaction guidance
- Audit artifact recipient and PGP key (if air-gapped)

Technical checklist for SRE/infra review (internal):
- Network: IP ranges, ports (443 + ephemeral model ports), metrics scrapers allowed hosts.
- Identity: KMS/HSM integration plan, key rotation cadence, secrets scope.
- Observability: optional telemetry endpoints, sample log redaction config, and retention SLA.
- Model & runtime: quantization profile, model artifact hash verification steps, fallback variant mapping.
- Backups: config for checkpoint snapshots and who has access.

Competitive notes — short differentiated positioning vs 3 archetypes:
1) Cloud-only LLM API vendors: they emphasize speed-to-ship but have limited private options. Our framing: same API, but we let you pick custody model + clear SLA.
2) Self-built inference stacks: cheaper on paper, but higher ops and slower model iteration. Our framing: drop-in runtime + professional services + handover pack reduces ops lift and exit friction.
3) Appliance / hardware vendors: physical isolation vs our flexible VPC/on-prem tradeoffs. Our framing: more deployment modes, faster policy iteration, and built-in rollback/fallback.

Discovery question bank (to use in first 45m call):
- Who are the stakeholders for procurement, audit, and infra? (names, not titles)
- What is the worst-case regulatory requirement that would kill the pilot? (data residency, export rules, model provenance)
- Do you require on-site review or is artefact-based evidence ok?
- Existing crypto/KMS vendors we must integrate with? HSM required?
- Expected request rates / token patterns for the pilot app?

Meeting prep — 5 min speaker bullets for AE/SE:
- Intro (30s): state pilot scope in 1 sentence.
- Security (2m): control-plane options and audit artifacts.
- Economics (2m): how we model unit cost and where reserved capacity wins.
- Pilot mechanics (1m): timeline + success metrics.
- Ask (30s): agree to pilot duration and 2 technical contacts.

Sample rebuttal scripts — quick pasteables for chat:
- "Telemetry is optional — we can ship signed artifacts instead."
- "You own the VPC endpoint and keys; our control plane is advisory unless you choose managed mode."
- "Pilot includes a handover pack so exit is straightforward and auditable."

Notes to self / open questions (do not share externally):
- Need final wording for "control plane is advisory" that legal signs off on.
- Confirm list of SOC2 artifacts we can provide automatically vs on-request.
- Engineering TODO: add a pilot-only flag to disable telemetry at runtime (config + deploy blueprint).
- Pricing TODO: create a 3-line item pilot invoice template (setup, compute reserve, optional managed ops).

Next steps (internal):
- Draft legal-approved paragraph for control-plane language (owner: Sabrina). Due 2025-11-14.
- SE/Ravi to prototype telemetry-off deployment and generate sample artifact bundle. Due 2025-11-21.
- AE team to test 3 sample email templates across two upcoming regulated prospects and collect feedback.

Appendix: Example pilot timeline (calendar weeks)
W0: NDA + high-level kickoff (contacts, network plan)
W1–W4: Integration (VPC peering / VPN, key config, model artifact transfer, smoke tests)
W5–W8: Traffic validation (real traffic or replay), audit artifact validation, cost/latency measurement
W8+: Handover, optional extended support or convert to Reserved Dedicated contract

End of doc.
